the C-terminal 10 amino acids of CotEs and a region between amino acids 37 and 160 are important for assembly of spore coat proteins into the outer coat layer.
the C-terminal 37 amino acids of Cot E are required for assembly of the outer coat and the C-terminal 10 amino acids are required for assembly and/or stability of CotB and CotG.
the C terminus of CotE and a region between amino acids 5 and 160 are required for the assembly of the outer layer of the Bacillus spore coat.

understanding the mechanism by which CotE assembles the outer layer of the spore coat and how CotE is involved in the assembly of other spore coat proteins.

the assembly of the spore coat and the morphogenetic role played by a coat protein, CotE.

the C-terminal 37 amino acids of CotEs are involved in the assembly of outer coat proteins.

the C-terminal 10 amino acids of CotA and the C-terminal 37 amino acids of CotC are required for outer coat protein localization and that the C termini of CotB and CotG are involved in their assembly into the coat.

CotE has a C-terminal domain that is important in outer coat morphogenesis, a central domain that is important for CotE localization, and an N-terminal domain that may play a role in CotE assembly into the outer coat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CotE plays a critical role in the assembly and/or stabilization of a set of outer coat proteins, and this role is not dependent on the presence of the C-terminal 37 amino acids of CotC.
CotE is involved in multiple aspects of coat morphogenesis and that it may play a role in the assembly and/or stabilization of the spore coat’s innermost layer, as well.
CotE has a role in the assembly, or stabilization, of the spore coat outer layer.
